# FDG8090

> DO apply a link demand to `ISerializable.GetObjectData` implementation. This ensures that only fully trusted assemblies and the Runtime Serializer have access to the member.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.10 Serialization.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Analyzer candidate rejected: link demands belong to Code Access Security, which .NET Core does not support (SecurityPermissionAttribute is obsolete there, SYSLIB0003); the Barton annotation keeps the rule for the platforms that have Code Access Security and application domains, which a check could not tell from a multi-targeted project's code.

## From the book

```csharp
[Serializable]
public class Person : ISerializable {
  [SecurityPermission(
   SecurityAction.LinkDemand,
   Flags = SecurityPermissionFlag.SerializationFormatter)
]
  void ISerializable.GetObjectData(...) {
    ...
  }
}
```

> **Jeremy Barton:** Link demands are part of the now-deprecated Code Access Security (CAS) system. The guidance may feel antiquated, but since the platforms that support CAS and the platforms that support AppDomains are the same, it’s still something you should do when using the `ISerializable` interface.
